Weak 'Soft Skills' Hurt Productivity, Employers Say

card.topic_en: Weak Soft Skills Hurt Workplace Productivity
card.summary_en: This lesson explores how weak soft skills impact workplace productivity, AI's role in hiring, and the importance of developing communication skills. It examines why interpersonal and communication skills are essential for modern workers alongside technical abilities.

vocab.definition_en: Personal attributes that enable someone to interact effectively and harmoniously with other people.
vocab.example: Good soft skills are essential for successful teamwork.

vocab.definition_en: The state or quality of being productive, especially in manufacturing goods or services.
vocab.example: New tools can help boost daily office productivity.

vocab.definition_en: The ability to convey information effectively and efficiently to others.
vocab.example: Strong communication skills can prevent misunderstandings at work.

vocab.definition_en: Relating to relationships or communication between people.
vocab.example: Interpersonal conflicts can ruin a great team dynamic.

vocab.definition_en: Work jointly on an activity or project to produce something.
vocab.example: We need to collaborate closely to finish the project.

vocab.definition_en: A person or organization that employs people.
vocab.example: Employers are looking for candidates with strong problem-solving abilities.

vocab.definition_en: Employ someone for wages or a salary.
vocab.example: The company decided to hire three new interns this month.

questions: Have you ever worked with someone who had great technical skills but poor communication?
Why do you think some employers struggle to find candidates with strong soft skills?
Do you consider yourself better at technical tasks or working with people?
How can companies help their employees improve their communication and teamwork skills?
Do you think artificial intelligence will change what employers look for in soft skills?

title: Celltrion Launches Omlyclo in U.S., Wins Spot on Major PBM Formulary

card.summary_en: Celltrion has launched its treatment Omlyclo in the U.S. and secured a spot on a major PBM formulary. This positions the company to utilize its first-mover advantage and improve patient access in the world's largest pharmaceutical market.

vocab.definition_en: A biologic medical product that is almost an identical copy of an original product.
vocab.example: The new biosimilar is much cheaper than the original drug.

vocab.definition_en: Introduce a new product or service to the market.
vocab.example: The pharmaceutical company plans to launch a new vaccine next month.

vocab.definition_en: Relating to the medicinal drugs or their preparation, use, or sale.
vocab.example: The pharmaceutical industry invests heavily in research and development.

vocab.definition_en: A list of prescription drugs covered by a health insurance plan.
vocab.example: Getting listed on the formulary is crucial for drug sales.

vocab.definition_en: An asset or object bought or obtained, typically by a library or museum.
vocab.example: The wholesale acquisition cost was lower than expected.

vocab.definition_en: The protection given by an insurance policy.
vocab.example: Patients hope the new medication will qualify for insurance coverage.

vocab.definition_en: A person or thing acting or serving in place of another.
vocab.example: Pharmacies can substitute the generic drug for the brand-name one.

questions: Have you ever had to buy expensive medicine and worry about insurance coverage?
Why do you think pharmaceutical companies try so hard to enter the US market?
What are the benefits of choosing a generic or biosimilar medicine over an original brand?
How does having a first-mover advantage change the dynamic in a competitive market?
Do you think healthcare systems should make it easier for biosimilars to replace original drugs?

title: The joy of foraging your own food

card.topic_en: The Joy of Foraging Wild Food
card.summary_en: Alexis Nikole Nelson shares the joy of foraging wild edible plants right in our neighborhoods. She emphasizes that paying closer attention to our environment can reconnect us with nature and our communities.

vocab.definition_en: Search widely for food or provisions in the wild.
vocab.example: Learning how to forage for mushrooms requires expert knowledge.

vocab.definition_en: Fit or suitable to be eaten; not poisonous.
vocab.example: Not all bright berries in the forest are edible.

vocab.definition_en: A district, especially one living in the same locality.
vocab.example: She loves finding wild herbs right in her own neighborhood.

vocab.definition_en: Restore a connection to someone or something.
vocab.example: Gardening helps people reconnect with the natural world.

vocab.definition_en: The scientific study of plants, including their physiology and structure.
vocab.example: His interest in botany led him to study forest ecosystems.

vocab.definition_en: The surroundings or conditions in which a person, animal, or plant lives.
vocab.example: We must protect our local environment from pollution.

vocab.definition_en: Recognize the full worth of something or someone.
vocab.example: Walking outdoors helps me appreciate the beauty of changing seasons.

questions: Have you ever tried picking wild berries, herbs, or plants in nature?
What is the most unusual food you have ever tried or seen growing outside?
Why do you think modern people are becoming more interested in foraging and outdoor hobbies?
How does spending time noticing plants in your neighborhood change your daily mood?
Would you trust yourself to eat wild plants found near a city street, or is it too risky?

title: Average American Rates Their Home 7.5 Out of 10

card.summary_en: This article explores the average rating that Americans give to their homes and the reasons for their satisfaction. It also examines what homeowners value most about their living spaces.

vocab.definition_en: To assign a value or rating to something based on quality.
vocab.example: How would you rate your current living space?

vocab.definition_en: The good feeling you have when you achieve or possess something.
vocab.example: Home satisfaction is important for mental health.

vocab.definition_en: A feeling of displeasure or disappointment with something.
vocab.example: High rent can cause major dissatisfaction among tenants.

vocab.definition_en: A person who owns their own home.
vocab.example: Many homeowners like to renovate their kitchens.

vocab.definition_en: The area or room where someone lives.
vocab.example: My living space is small but very cozy.

vocab.definition_en: To consider something as important or useful.
vocab.example: I value natural light in my apartment.

vocab.definition_en: An explanation or cause that happens frequently.
vocab.example: Location is a common reason for buying a house.

questions: What score would you give to your current home out of ten?
What are the most important features you look for in a living space?
Why do you think location matters so much when choosing a home?
How does the design of your room affect your daily mood and productivity?
What changes would you make to your home if you had an unlimited budget?

title: VR Project Brings Hope to Kids in Japan Hospitals

card.topic_en: VR Project Brings Hope to Kids
card.summary_en: A virtual reality project in Japan provides hospitalized children with the chance to explore virtual worlds. Through this, kids find hope and stay connected during long hospital stays.

vocab.definition_en: Admitted to a hospital for treatment.
vocab.example: The hospitalized children really enjoyed the VR experience.

vocab.definition_en: An artificial environment created with computer technology.
vocab.example: Virtual reality can take you to places you have never visited.

vocab.definition_en: An online or computer-simulated environment.
vocab.example: Exploring a virtual world is a great way to escape boredom.

vocab.definition_en: To join or link together with others.
vocab.example: Technology helps patients connect with their friends outside.

vocab.definition_en: The period of time someone spends receiving care in a hospital.
vocab.example: Long hospital stays can be very stressful for young kids.

vocab.definition_en: To discover a feeling of optimism about the future.
vocab.example: Programs like this help patients find hope during hard times.

vocab.definition_en: To travel through an unfamiliar area in order to learn about it.
vocab.example: Kids love to explore new places using headsets.

questions: Have you ever tried using a virtual reality headset before?
How do you usually pass the time when you are sick in bed?
In what ways can technology improve the lives of sick children?
Where would you like to visit first if you put on a VR headset?
Do you think immersive technology should be used more often in modern hospitals?

title: Osaka Metro Tests AI Robot Station Worker

card.topic_en: Osaka Metro Tests AI Robot Worker
card.summary_en: Osaka Metro is testing an AI robot station worker that assists passengers and answers questions. This project explores the future roles of robots in public transit.

vocab.definition_en: To try something out to see how well it works.
vocab.example: The company will test a new robot at the station.

vocab.definition_en: An employee who works at a transportation station.
vocab.example: The station worker helped me buy a train ticket.

vocab.definition_en: To give support or help to someone.
vocab.example: AI robots can assist tourists with translation.

vocab.definition_en: A person traveling in a vehicle, train, or plane.
vocab.example: Passengers waited patiently on the platform.

vocab.definition_en: A system of transport for passengers by group travel.
vocab.example: Public transit in this city is very efficient.

vocab.definition_en: The function assumed or part played by a person or thing.
vocab.example: Robots will play a big role in future workplaces.

vocab.definition_en: To provide information in response to inquiries.
vocab.example: Chatbots are designed to answer questions quickly.

questions: Have you ever interacted with a robot or chatbot at a train station?
What are the benefits of having robot workers in public places?
Would you feel comfortable asking a robot for directions in a busy station?
What jobs do you think robots should take over in the near future?
Do you prefer dealing with human customer service or automated machines?

title: Reading for Pleasure Improves Well-being

card.summary_en: This article explores how reading for pleasure at any age supports mental, emotional, and social well-being. It also explains how regular reading helps reduce the risk of cognitive decline.

vocab.definition_en: The state of being comfortable, healthy, or happy.
vocab.example: Regular reading greatly improves your mental well-being.

vocab.definition_en: A gradual loss of brain function and memory.
vocab.example: Reading daily can prevent cognitive decline as we age.

vocab.definition_en: A feeling of happy satisfaction and enjoyment.
vocab.example: She reads books purely for pleasure on weekends.

vocab.definition_en: To make something smaller or less in amount or degree.
vocab.example: Good books help reduce stress after work.

vocab.definition_en: To give assistance, comfort, or encouragement to someone.
vocab.example: Libraries support lifelong learning in communities.

vocab.definition_en: Relating to the mind or the processes of the mind.
vocab.example: Taking breaks is important for mental health.

vocab.definition_en: A situation involving exposure to danger or loss.
vocab.example: Healthy habits lower the risk of illness.

questions: Do you usually read books for fun, or only when you have to for work or school?
What was the last book you read, and did you actually enjoy it?
How do you usually feel after spending an hour reading a good book?
Do you think reading fiction or non-fiction is better for improving your well-being?
Why do you think many people find it hard to read books regularly nowadays?

title: Worker in 70s Falls to Death at Incheon Snack Factory

card.summary_en: A worker in their 70s tragically died after falling into a freight elevator shaft at an Incheon snack factory. Authorities have launched investigations into this and other fatal workplace accidents across the country.

vocab.definition_en: An occurrence of death by accident, disease, or war.
vocab.example: The factory had a tragic workplace fatality yesterday.

vocab.definition_en: A post-mortem examination to discover the cause of death.
vocab.example: Police will request an autopsy to determine the cause.

vocab.definition_en: The action of investigating something or a formal inquiry.
vocab.example: An official investigation into the accident has begun.

vocab.definition_en: To act in accordance with a wish or command.
vocab.example: Companies must strictly comply with safety regulations.

vocab.definition_en: To temporarily prevent from continuing or being effective.
vocab.example: The ministry ordered work at the site suspended.

vocab.definition_en: A general rule, principle, or piece of advice.
vocab.example: Safety guidelines are essential in every workplace.

vocab.definition_en: To fall down or fall in suddenly.
vocab.example: Old structures can collapse without proper maintenance.

questions: Have you ever worked in a place where safety rules were very strict?
Why do you think workplace accidents still happen so frequently in some industries?
What responsibilities should factory owners have to protect older daily workers?
How can the government effectively force companies to follow safety guidelines?
Do you think severe punishments for company CEOs can prevent industrial accidents?

title: Mister Donut Returns to China for First Time Since 2019

card.summary_en: This article covers Mister Donut returning to the Chinese market for the first time since 2019. It looks at how the popular Japanese donut chain is expanding its business across Asia.

vocab.definition_en: To become or make larger or more extensive.
vocab.example: The famous brand plans to expand into new markets.

vocab.definition_en: A series of businesses owned by the same company.
vocab.example: Mister Donut is a well-known international chain.

vocab.definition_en: To come or go back to a place or person.
vocab.example: Fans are excited about the brand's return to China.

vocab.definition_en: Liked or admired by many people or a particular person.
vocab.example: Japanese bakeries are very popular among young adults.

vocab.definition_en: A regular gathering of people for the purchase and sale of provisions.
vocab.example: Entering the Chinese market requires a smart strategy.

vocab.definition_en: To introduce a new product or service to the public.
vocab.example: They will launch a new seasonal menu next month.

vocab.definition_en: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term goal.
vocab.example: Their business strategy focuses on trendy desserts.

questions: What is your favorite donut or bakery brand, and why do you like it?
Have you ever tried Mister Donut when traveling or in your home country?
Why do you think foreign food chains are often very successful in Asian cities?
How important is social media marketing when a restaurant brand enters a new country?
If you could bring any international food brand to your neighborhood, which one would it be?
